current_statement: A redis-wait-quorum tier's quorum and timeout_ms are bounded below (>= 1) but not above in both the parser and the layer-A state guard, so an operator value such as redis-wait-quorum:4294967295:<huge> classifies as a legal SharedRedis state and sizes the Redis client response deadline (timeout_ms + 2s) and the WAIT timeout to effectively unbounded, turning a fail-closed refusal into an indefinite admission hang.
current_title: The redis-wait-quorum quorum and timeout_ms have no upper bound in the parser or the layer-A guard, so an absurd timeout makes the admission await effectively unbounded
evidence: Still no upper bound anywhere. ReplayDurabilityTier::parse filters only `quorum >= 1` and `timeout_ms >= 1` (mcp-re-proxy/src/replay_tier.rs:101-118); the layer-A state guard wait_quorum_guards refuses only 0 for either (config_state/replay.rs:227-245); materialization passes tier.wait_quorum_params() straight into RedisAsyncAtomicReplayStore::connect_with_wait_quorum (replay_plane/backends.rs:104-110). The store sizes the client response timeout as timeout_ms.saturating_add(2_000) (async_redis_store.rs:212-223), so an absurd declared timeout yields an effectively unbounded client deadline and a WAIT that can hold an admission await for that long; an absurd quorum makes every admission wait the full timeout and refuse. Configuration-only (no remote lever); the stall direction is fail-closed but a huge timeout converts refusal into an indefinite hang on the admission path.
